messages:
meera: quick question — i'm about to add a terraform change to let pods in namespace `payments` decrypt a KMS key via IRSA. want to make sure i'm wiring the key policy vs grant vs role policy correctly. planning something like below, does this look safe?

meera: terraform snippet i was going to apply:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "payments_irsa" {
  name = "payments-irsa-role"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "payments_key" {
  description = "payments service key (pods)"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "payments_decrypt_grant" {
  name = "payments-decrypt-grant"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.payments_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.payments_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

meera: main concerns: 1) do i need explicit key policy allowing the role, or is the kms_grant sufficient? 2) can we add an encryption context condition to the grant? 3) any pitfalls with IRSA role arn vs OIDC-subject matching?

chris: short answers: 1) kms_grant is often enough for runtime decrypt, but best practice is to have key policy that at least allows the account root to administer and optionally a statement granting Encrypt/Decrypt to the role. grants are ephemeral-ish and tied to the principal — fine for short-lived access but harder to audit.

chris: for more durable control and obvious audit trail, put a key policy statement like:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowIRSA-decrypt",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/payments-irsa-role" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {
      "aws:PrincipalTag/team": "payments"
    }
  }
}
```

alex: +1 to chris. also note: if you rely on a grant, terraform will create a `aws_kms_grant` resource but it can be revoked by the KMS service if the grantee loses principal (role deleted). key policy ensures admins can still reason about access.

meera: thanks. wanted to add an encryption context check so only pods that set a specific EK tag can decrypt. can that go into the grant or only the role policy?

chris: you can put conditions on the key policy using `kms:EncryptionContext:someKey` and also on IAM policies. Grants support `constraints` block but support is limited in terraform provider versions — iirc you can set `constraints = { encryption_context_subset = { "purpose": "payments-storage" } }` in `aws_kms_grant` but double-check provider version.

meera: ah ok — here's what i was thinking for the pod/serviceaccount side. remind me if this is the right OIDC annotation form:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: payments-sa
  namespace: payments
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/payments-irsa-role
```

jordan: that's the right annotation. also ensure your IAM role trust policy is the OIDC provider with the correct `sub` condition like:
```json
"Condition": {"StringEquals": {"sts:ExternalId": "redwood-payments"}}
```

jordan: actually — for IRSA you usually do:
```json
"Condition": {"StringEquals": {"token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub": "system:serviceaccount:payments:payments-sa"}}
```

chris: small correction — the key thing is the `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` flow. trust policy should allow the OIDC provider `aud` and `sub` as needed. external id isn't used for IRSA typically.

meera: got it. i'll remove external id. any concerns about terraform plan ordering? i worry the grant will reference the role ARN that doesn't exist yet because k8s SA creation is separate.

alex: terraform only manages aws resources. service account is created via k8s provider/apply. order: create IAM role & trust policy, create KMS key and key policy, then kms_grant referencing role. That's fine. If SA doesn't exist in aws, role can still be created. The trust policy references OIDC subject string, not the k8s SA resource itself.

meera: makes sense. last Q: should we scope the role ARN in key policy or use tags/conditions instead to be less brittle across envs?

chris: prefer conditions/tags so you don't have to update key policy per role rename. e.g. tag role with `team=payments` and add `StringEquals: {"aws:PrincipalTag/team": "payments"}` in key policy. Much easier for infra drift.

meera: perfect — i'll implement key policy with principal tag condition + a kms_grant with encryption_context constraint (and bump provider if needed). will ping when i open the PR. :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: terraform plan (module.payments.kms) completed — 1 add, 2 change, 0 destroy. (mocked run for staging)

meera: thanks — i'll open PR and add a short note in PR description about the grant vs key policy rationale.

alex: thumbs up. if you want i can review the PR for provider quirks.

meera: please do — tagging you in the PR when it's up.
